questions.q: What is the main point of the article?
options: Iran is compensating war victims fairly with seized property
Iran is seizing assets of critics abroad and their relatives
Iran's courts are protecting diaspora property from confiscation
Iranian banks are collapsing after the war with Israel
questions.explain: The regime is confiscating property of those abroad, and of relatives at home, as punishment for dissent.

questions.q: Why were the Najafiragheb couple's assets frozen?
options: They sold family property to relatives living abroad
Their daughter's social media posts opposing the government
They attended anti-government protests with their son
Their son worked for the channel Iran International
questions.explain: The punishment was for the social media posts of their daughter Noushin in Europe.

questions.q: How many people outside Iran had had assets seized, according to Iranian media in April?
options: Over 1,400
Over 400
Over 40
Over 4,000
questions.explain: Iranian outlets reported seizures against over 400 people abroad.

questions.q: What did official Mohammad Kazemifard say about the new electronic system?
options: It required judges to approve each seizure within 400 days
It was used only to seize businesses owned by journalists
It cut a process of up to 400 days to a few clicks
It raised the time needed to seize property to 400 days
questions.explain: He said a process that took up to 400 days now takes only a few clicks.

questions.q: What does lawyer Saeid Dehghan suggest about the seizures?
options: They target mainly the very famous
They will soon stop
They are a message to the wider diaspora
They are aimed at five specific individuals
questions.explain: He says the message is directed at a much wider Iranian diaspora, not just five people.
